title: NSE raises Rs 6,746 Cr from anchor investors ahead of IPO
summary:
The National Stock Exchange (NSE) has raised Rs 6,746 crore from anchor investors ahead of its much-awaited initial public offering (IPO), which opens for public subscription today (September 17).
The exchange allotted 3.78 crore equity shares to 189 anchor investors at Rs 1,785 per share, the upper end of its IPO price band.
The anchor book saw participation from several large domestic and global investors, including Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA), GIC Singapore, Fidelity, Societe Generale and others.
LIC emerged as the largest single anchor investor, picking up shares worth around Rs 400 crore. The Government Pension Fund Global invested about Rs 250 crore, while Societe Generale’s offshore desk bought shares worth nearly Rs 316 crore.
Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) invested around Rs 2,883 crore, accounting for nearly 43% of the anchor book. Domestic investors contributed around Rs 3,588 crore, or 53% of the allocation. The domestic participation included more than 25 mutual funds and 11 large insurance and pension funds.
The anchor book attracted bids worth nearly Rs 1.2 lakh crore, around 20 times the amount allocated to anchor investors, according to market sources.
NSE has set a price band of Rs 1,700-1,785 per share for its IPO, which will remain open until September 21. The issue is entirely an offer for sale (OFS), meaning NSE will not receive any fresh capital from the IPO. Instead, existing shareholders will sell their shares.
The exchange is looking to raise around Rs 22,569 crore through the IPO, making it one of India's largest public issues.

title: RentoMojo makes stock market debut at 19% premium
summary:
Furniture and appliance rental platform RentoMojo made its stock market debut on Thursday, September 17, with its shares listing at a nearly 19% premium over the IPO issue price.
The company’s shares opened at Rs 482.45 on the NSE, compared with the issue price of Rs 404, marking a 19.42% premium. On the BSE, the stock debuted at Rs 480, translating into an 18.81% premium.
The listing comes after strong investor demand for RentoMojo’s Rs 1,256 crore IPO. The issue was subscribed 72.87 times, with the qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) portion receiving bids worth around 177.3 times the shares on offer. The non-institutional investor (NII) portion was subscribed 67.92 times, while the retail portion saw 15.58 times subscription.
RentoMojo had fixed the IPO price band at Rs 384-404 per share. The issue comprised a fresh issue of Rs 150 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) worth around Rs 1,106 crore. This means nearly 88% of the issue came from existing shareholders selling their shares, while the company raised Rs 150 crore in fresh capital.
The Bengaluru-based company operates a rental platform for furniture and home appliances, allowing consumers to rent products through monthly subscriptions. It caters mainly to urban households and operates across major Indian cities.
RentoMojo competes with players such as Pepperfry, Furlenco and Cityfurnish. With its listing, the company has become the first in its segment to hit the IPO market.
Earlier, Entrackr reported that several early RentoMojo investors are set to generate significant returns through the IPO, with some early backers expected to clock up to 152X returns on their OFS.
On the financial front, RentoMojo’s revenue from operations grew 45.5% year-on-year to Rs 387 crore in FY26. Its profit after tax jumped 142% to Rs 104.2 crore, compared with Rs 43.1 crore in FY25
The share price of Rentomojo is currently trading at Rs 502 (as of 10.12 AM), with a total market capitalisation of Rs 5,250 crore ($535 million).

title: Inside Yulu’s Series C: funding breakup, valuation, captable
summary:
Electric mobility-as-a-service (MaaS) platform Yulu recently raised $93 million in its Series C round through a mix of debt and equity. The round comprised $63 million in equity led by GEF Capital Partners, with participation from One Planet Partners, and $30 million in debt.
Entrackr examined Yulu's regulatory filings to decode the company's latest funding round, updated captable, and post-money valuation. 
According to the company’s regulatory filings accessed from the Registrar of Companies (RoC),Yulu board approved 200 equity shares and 55,200 Series C compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 82,615 per share to raise Rs 456 crore.
Separately, the company issued 10,770 Series C1 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 84,291 to raise Rs 91 crore. Combined, Yulu raised around Rs 547 crore through the equity funding.
According to the filings, the proposed debt component has yet to be received, while the transaction also involves a secondary component.
GEF Capital Partners led the series C round with an investment of Rs 456 crore and remaining amount infused by One Planet Partners Rs 91 crore.
As per the filing, Yulu plans to deploy the fresh capital to strengthen its capital base, support operations and strategic initiatives, and fuel future growth. The company aims to quadruple its active fleet to 200,000 electric vehicles over the next two years, expand into new urban mobility use cases, and support its potential public market listing plans.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, Yulu’s post-money valuation stood at around $180–200 million.
Founded in 2017 by Amit Gupta, Anuj Tewari, RK Misra, and Naveen Dachuri, Yulu operates a technology-enabled fleet of electric two-wheelers for urban mobility and last-mile delivery. Its fleet is currently around 50,000 vehicles, with the company planning to expand its presence to about 20 cities over the next year.
Following the latest allotment, GEF Capital Partners acquired a 31.29% stake in Yulu, followed by Magna International Inc. at 14.38% and Bajaj Auto at 12.38%. One Planet Partners holds a 6.13% stake. Yulu’s co-founders collectively retain a 22.25% stake in the company, with Amit Gupta holding 8.90%, while Naveen Dachuri, Rajendra Kumar Misra and Hemant Gupta each hold 4.45%.

Bengaluru-based Yulu is yet to file its FY26 financials. In its latest available FY25 filings, the company’s operating revenue jumped 98% to Rs 237.4 Cr, from Rs 120 Cr in FY24, while its net loss decreased 12% to Rs 126 Cr, from Rs 142.8 Cr.

title: Peak XV sells 1.47% stake in Groww for Rs 1,756 Cr via bulk deal
summary:
Peak XV Partners has offloaded a 1.47% stake in Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent company of stockbroking platform Groww, through a bulk deal on Wednesday.
According to bulk deal data, Peak XV Partners Investments VI-1 sold 9.17 crore shares at an average price of Rs 191.49 apiece. The transaction was valued at around Rs 1,756 crore.
As of June 2026, Peak XV Partners Investments VI-1 held a 15.68% stake in Groww, which made it one of the company’s largest institutional shareholders. Based on the June shareholding, the latest sale represents nearly a tenth of its holding in the company.
The transaction comes less than a month after two of Groww’s early investors, Y Combinator and Ribbit Capital, pared their stakes through large open-market transactions.
In August, Y Combinator, through YC Holdings II, sold nearly 7.47 crore shares, or a 1.2% stake, for around Rs 1,435 crore. Later that month, Ribbit Capital offloaded 11.31 crore shares  for Rs 2,217 crore.
Together, Y Combinator and Ribbit Capital sold shares worth more than Rs 3,650 crore in August. Including Peak XV’s latest transaction, the three investors have offloaded Groww shares worth over Rs 5,400 crore since August.
Peak XV had also trimmed its holding in Groww earlier this year. In May, the investment firm sold 6.2 crore shares for around Rs 1,116 crore.
On the financial front, Groww recorded Rs 1,501 crore in operating revenue during Q1 FY27, a 66% year-on-year increase. Its net profit nearly doubled to Rs 735 crore during the same period.
Following the transaction, Groww’s shares fell nearly 4% on Wednesday to close at Rs 189.76, giving the company a market capitalization of around Rs 1.19 lakh crore ($12.5 billion).

title: Zeropearl VC leads Rs 11.4 Cr seed round in aesthetic surgery platform TRUE ARTIS
summary:
Integrated aesthetic surgery platform TRUE ARTIS has raised Rs 11.4 crore in a seed funding round led by Zeropearl VC. The round also saw participation from Eleven, a diversified business group of Sunil Sachdeva, co-founder of Medanta, and a group of angel investors.
The round saw participation from operators and healthcare investors including Arjun Vaidya, Dhruv Joshi, Ambarish Gupta and Vivek Lohcheb, CBO of PhonePe, along with former senior executives from Airtel and OYO.
The fresh funds will be used to open two new centres in Delhi NCR over the next six to eight months, strengthen its surgical and recovery capabilities, expand its network of plastic and aesthetic surgeons, and enhance its technology and patient-care systems, TRUE ARTIS said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2025 by Ankit Joshi and Sandeep Upadhyay, TRUE ARTIS is an integrated aesthetic surgery platform focused on personalised aesthetic care. The startup brings together plastic and aesthetic surgeons, surgical infrastructure, hospital-grade safety protocols, dedicated recovery facilities and a privacy-focused patient experience.
TRUE ARTIS offers services across facial aesthetics, breast procedures, body contouring, hair restoration and non-surgical treatments. Its in-house technology platform manages the patient journey from enquiry and consultation through surgery and recovery.
The company claims to have served more than 10,000 clients and completed over 400 surgeries in the past nine months. Its centres feature operating theatres, surgical and medical equipment, dedicated recovery facilities, ICU backup and private patient suites.
TRUE ARTIS also works with a multidisciplinary network of full-time and visiting plastic surgeons, allowing patients to access multiple specialists through a single platform. It currently operates two centres in Delhi and Gurgaon.
The startup works with around 20 plastic surgeons across Delhi NCR and reports a 98% client satisfaction rate. It said its first centre has reached EBITDA break-even, while revenue is growing at a double-digit rate month-on-month.

title: super.money appoints former BharatPe CPO Rohan Khara as Chief Product Officer
summary:
Fintech platform super.money has appointed Rohan Khara as its Chief Product Officer (CPO) as the company looks to expand its product offerings across payments, credit and commerce.
Entrackr had exclusively reported in June that Khara had stepped down as CPO of BharatPe. He brings close to two decades of experience across product management, financial services and consumer technology, with senior roles at BharatPe, FairMoney, Gojek and MobiKwik.
At BharatPe, Khara served as CPO, where he led product development across the company's merchant and consumer businesses. Before joining BharatPe, he was Managing Director, India at FairMoney and had earlier served as its CPO for Nigeria and India.
Khara was also part of the founding team of Gojek's financial services business in Jakarta, where he worked on building financial products for emerging markets. His experience spans India, Indonesia and Nigeria, with a focus on financial services and consumer technology products.
"super.money has built strong momentum by challenging the traditional role of a payments app. We are now at an important inflection point, where we are focusing on building a broader financial platform that can create value for consumers across how they pay, borrow and shop," said Prakash Sikaria, founder and CEO of super.money.
Khara said he plans to build on super.money's consumer proposition and develop products across UPI, credit and commerce.

title: Semiconductor verification startup VerifAIX raises $5 Mn in seed round
summary:
AI-native semiconductor verification startup VerifAIX has raised $5 million in a seed funding round co-led by Endiya Partners and Bluehill VC.
The proceeds will be used for product development, customer deployments and expansion of its engineering teams across the US, India and Israel, VerifAIX said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2024 by Madhulima Tewari, Kenneth Roe and Avner Landver, VerifAIX is building an AI-native verification platform for semiconductor design. It helps engineering teams verify increasingly complex chips with greater speed and rigor.
VerifAIX’s platform combines AI with formal methods to create a verification trust layer that connects design specifications, RTL and verification assets. This enables traceable verification from design intent to closure.
The startup’s “Formal Brain” creates a mathematically grounded understanding of a design and its intended behaviour. It reasons across specifications, RTL and verification assets to identify inconsistencies and gaps, and uses this foundation for verification planning, formal analysis, simulation, coverage, debug and verification closure.
VerifAIX integrates specification-to-RTL reasoning, automated decomposition and abstraction, and coordinated formal and simulation verification to tackle complex designs while maintaining traceability to design intent. It targets custom-silicon developers, including semiconductor and IP companies, processor and AI accelerator developers, hyperscalers and systems companies.
India’s semiconductor startup ecosystem is also seeing the emergence of AI-native verification platforms alongside the broader chip design boom.
Chennai-based deep-tech startup Vyoma Systems, incubated at IIT Madras Pravartak, is working on AI-driven pre-silicon verification through its UpTickPro platform. The platform integrates functional verification, FPGA validation, software bring-up and security analysis.
The development comes amid rising capital flows into Indian semiconductor startups. Companies raised $61.9 million in H1 2026, taking total funding since 2022 to about $206 million, according to a Speciale Invest and Startup Policy Forum report.
Recent funding rounds include BigEndian Semiconductors’ $6 million raise for its fabless SoC platform, while HrdWyr raised $13 million in Series A funding to develop AI-native SoCs.

title: Fashion discovery platform Slayd raises pre-seed funding led by ajvc

Gurugram-based fashion discovery platform Slayd has raised Rs 1.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by ajvc, an early-stage fund founded by Aviral Bhatnagar.
The round values the startup at around Rs 16.66 crore post-money. Slayd will use the funds to expand its team and scale its private-label business, Slayd Originals.
Founded in 2025 by IIT Roorkee alumni Sparsh Jain, Harsh Porwal and Kumar Prasang, Slayd aggregates fashion products from more than 300 marketplaces and D2C brands. The platform adds around 1 lakh new products every month and uses a proprietary model that evaluates products across more than eight signals to identify emerging trends.
The startup claims to have crossed 200,000 users, with over 40% month-one retention. Its power users average more than 10 sessions per month, while the platform currently identifies over 2,000 products as emerging hotsellers.
Slayd also curates products into theme-based collections and personalised feeds, allowing users to discover products across multiple fashion platforms.
The company has also entered the private-label segment with Slayd Originals, which was launched in beta earlier this year. The brand currently generates around 1,000 orders per month, according to the startup.
“India sees more than 1 lakh new apparel designs launched every month across hundreds of fragmented e-commerce platforms. Yet shoppers still have to navigate multiple platforms to discover what's actually trending. Slayd is building the discovery layer for this fragmented market,” said cofounder Sparsh Jain.
The startup said its product and trend data is also used to identify styles that could be developed under Slayd Originals.
“Our advantage is that we can identify what shoppers want before building it ourselves. By controlling the design and supply chain, we can bring high-demand styles to customers at better prices, with better quality and a more consistent shopping experience,” said cofounder Harsh Porwal.
With the latest funding, Slayd plans to expand its team and increase the scale of Slayd Originals.

title: PhonePe crosses 11 Bn monthly UPI transactions in August; G-Pay nears 8 Bn
summary:
PhonePe crossed the 11 billion monthly transaction mark on the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) in August, while Google Pay neared 8 billion transactions, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
PhonePe recorded 11.19 billion UPI transactions in August, compared to 10.86 billion in July. The Walmart-backed digital payments platform accounted for 45.64% of total UPI transaction volume. In value terms, PhonePe processed transactions worth Rs 14.26 lakh crore, giving it a 47.82% share of the total UPI transaction value.
Google Pay retained the second spot with 7.91 billion UPI transactions in August, compared to 7.65 billion in July. The platform held a 32.26% share of transaction volume and a 33.78% share by value. Its transaction value stood at Rs 10.07 lakh crore during the month.
Paytm remained the third-largest UPI player with 1.97 billion transactions in August against 1.90 billion in July. The fintech platform accounted for 8.03% of UPI transaction volume and 6.87% of transaction value. Its transaction value stood at Rs 2.05 lakh crore.

Navi retained the fourth position with 1.08 billion transactions in August against 947.08 million in July. Its volume share rose to 4.40%, while its value share stood at 1.76%. The platform processed transactions worth Rs 52,513 crore.
Flipkart-backed super.money recorded 421.87 million transactions in August against 437.27 million in July. BHIM recorded 253.69 million transactions, up from 242.27 million in the previous month.
FamApp by Trio recorded 223.31 million transactions in August, while WhatsApp registered 183.69 million transactions. WhatsApp remained ahead of CRED, which recorded 143.94 million transactions during the month.
CRED remained in the 10th position in August. Despite its lower transaction volume, CRED handled transactions worth Rs 57,398 crore and accounted for 1.92% of UPI transaction value. WhatsApp's transaction value stood at Rs 13,948 crore, giving it a 0.47% share.
Axis Bank's apps recorded 146.78 million transactions across customer-initiated, B2C and B2B payments. Their combined transaction value stood at Rs 14,024 crore.
Overall, UPI recorded 24.51 billion transactions worth Rs 29.82 lakh crore in August, compared with 23.66 billion transactions worth Rs 29.88 lakh crore in July.
PhonePe and Google Pay together accounted for 77.90% of total UPI transaction volume and 81.60% of transaction value in August. The top three players, PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm, accounted for 85.93% of UPI transaction volume and 88.47% of transaction value during the month.
Meanwhile, the new MDR framework could open a potential revenue stream for UPI apps such as PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm. From October 15, select P2M transactions above Rs 2,000 will attract a 0.4% MDR, capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above. The fee will be shared among participants across the UPI ecosystem, including banks, PSPs and payment apps.

title: Fibe gets SEBI nod for Rs 750 Cr IPO
summary:
Digital consumer lending platform Fibe, operated by Social Worth Technologies, has received SEBI’s nod to proceed with its proposed initial public offering (IPO).
The IPO will comprise a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 750 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 4.01 crore equity shares by existing shareholders, according to the company’s draft red herring prospectus (DRHP).
SEBI has issued its final observations on the proposed IPO, allowing Fibe to move ahead with the public issue process.
The company plans to use the net proceeds from the fresh issue to fund investments in its material subsidiary, EarlySalary Services Pvt Ltd (ESPL), to augment its capital base and meet its onward lending requirements. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.
The IPO-bound company reported Rs 1,585 crore in revenue from operations in FY26, up from Rs 1,209 crore in FY25. Its net profit more than doubled to Rs 257 crore from Rs 114 crore during the same period.
Interest on loans remained its largest revenue source, contributing nearly 65% of operating revenue, while fee and commission income stood at Rs 393.5 crore in FY26. Fibe also reported Rs 420 crore in impairment on financial instruments, including Rs 203 crore in loan write-offs.
Founded in 2015 by Akshay Mehrotra and Ashish Goyal, Fibe offers personal and purpose-led financing across areas including healthcare, education and solar rooftop installations. The company claims to have facilitated more than 9.8 million loans with cumulative disbursements exceeding Rs 48,000 crore.
Kotak Mahindra Capital Company, Axis Capital, DAM Capital Advisors and JM Financial are the book-running lead managers to the issue.
Fibe competes with Moneyview, which today halved its IPO size to Rs 750 crore. Another key competitor, Kissht, recently got listed and is currently trading at around Rs 340, nearly double its issue price.

title: NPCI sets 0.4% MDR on UPI above Rs 2,000, caps fee at Rs 300 for Rs 75,000 and higher transactions
summary:
The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has introduced a 0.4% Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on select Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000. The new framework will take effect from October 15, 2026.
For transactions of Rs 75,000 and above, the MDR will be capped at Rs 300 per transaction. This means merchants will not pay more than Rs 300 even if 0.4% of the transaction value exceeds that amount. For example, a Rs 1 lakh transaction would attract Rs 400 at the 0.4% rate, but the MDR payable will be limited to Rs 300.
UPI transactions of up to Rs 2,000 will continue to have zero MDR. According to NPCI's FAQ, such small-value transactions account for more than 95% of the total volume of UPI P2M transactions.
The charges will apply to merchants and not consumers. Users will continue to make UPI payments free of charge, while UPI app providers will not be allowed to levy a platform fee or any other charge on UPI payments.
Small vendors under the Person-to-Person Merchant (P2PM) framework will continue to be exempt from MDR. The framework covers small merchants receiving up to Rs 1 lakh per month through UPI QR codes directly into their accounts.
For select merchant categories such as railways, telecom services, insurance and fuel, a flat MDR of Rs 5 per transaction will apply to payments above Rs 2,000 instead of the 0.4% rate.
The framework also proposes a dedicated fund for small merchants to support digital payment infrastructure and merchant onboarding in Tier 3 to Tier 6 centres, including the Northeast, Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. The detailed framework is to be finalised in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) within three months.
NPCI said the MDR revenue will be distributed within the UPI ecosystem to support infrastructure resilience, innovation, cybersecurity and customer service.
The FAQ said UPI's MDR remains lower than traditional card-based payment fees. Standard credit card MDRs typically range from 1.5% to 2.5%, while debit card MDRs are capped at up to 0.9%.
Under the new structure, a Rs 3,000 transaction will attract Rs 12 MDR, while a Rs 50,000 transaction will attract Rs 200. Once the transaction value reaches Rs 75,000, the MDR is capped at Rs 300.

title: Teachers’ Venture Growth makes follow-on investment in Darwinbox
summary:
Teachers’ Venture Growth (TVG), the late-stage venture and growth investment platform of Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, has made a follow-on investment in human capital management (HCM) platform Darwinbox.
This marks TVG’s second investment in Darwinbox after its initial investment in the company in 2025. The financial details of the transaction were not disclosed.
Founded in 2015 by Jayant Paleti, Chaitanya Peddi, Rohit Chennamaneni and Vineet Singh, Darwinbox offers a mobile-first, cloud-based HCM platform that enables organisations to manage the employee lifecycle, from hiring and onboarding to talent management and retention.
The company has continued to invest in its HCM product suite, with a focus on workflow automation, streamlined HR operations and personalised employee experiences.
In August, Darwinbox launched Darwinbox Cortex, an AI-native HCM platform. The product was launched with pilot customers including Fortune 1000 companies Visteon and Transcarent.
Cortex brings AI-driven intelligence, context and execution into Darwinbox’s platform and is being developed with technology partners including Microsoft, Slack and Glean. The platform extends AI capabilities to applications and workflows used by employees.
Darwinbox said it serves more than 1,400 companies and 4.5 million employees globally. The company has grown at a 70% CAGR over the past five years, with expansion across key markets including the US, Middle East, India and Southeast Asia.

The round also saw participation from Claypond Capital, Martin Chavez, Olivier Pomel, Venky Harinarayan and Shah Rukh Khan, along with existing investors RTP Global and Dovetail.
Flam will use the fresh capital to expand R&D across its AI models, broaden its product suite and scale enterprise sales globally.
Founded in 2021 by Shourya Agarwal, Malhar Patil, and Amit Gaiki, Flam develops AI-powered interactive content for enterprises across use cases such as marketing, product visualisation, learning and development, entertainment, fan engagement, customer support and sales. The company said it has onboarded more than 100 enterprise customers in the past six quarters, including Google, Reliance and Hyundai.
Flam currently holds more than 15 patents and offers three core formats. Its Flicks product enables interactive videos that can switch people, products or scenes during playback. The company said Flicks uses a patented compression algorithm and is delivered programmatically with a 50-millisecond time-to-first-buffer.
Its Forge editing model uses image references to modify specified elements, while Airboards provides high-fidelity 3D content through a camera interface with touch, voice and haptic interactions. Flam said its 3D streaming technology can load Airboards in 300 milliseconds without requiring users to install an app. Its Fable image-to-video model generates assets as native alpha-channel videos.
Flam is also developing Visual Agents, human-like characters designed to conduct conversations and take agentic actions. The technology combines Fantom for facial expression, identity preservation and motion transfer; Finesse for multilingual voice capabilities; and Falcon, a 26-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts large language model. The company said its pipeline can return an answer in under two seconds, with Falcon delivering a 30-millisecond time-to-first-token.
Headquartered in San Francisco, Flam has teams in India and Japan. The company said it has five AI models, more than 15 patents and over 100 enterprise customers globally.

title: India’s wealthtech funding frenzy continues in 2026 as investment crosses $300 Mn
summary:
India’s wealthtech ecosystem is attracting stronger investor interest in 2026, with funding increasingly flowing towards platforms expanding beyond traditional broking and trading. Investors are showing greater appetite for digital wealth management, alternative investments, fixed income products and technology led advisory platforms, while a new crop of startups is targeting younger, first time investors. However, the sector remains largely concentrated in Tier 1 cities, with both wealthtech startups and their user base skewed towards major urban centres. This leaves sizable headroom for platforms to expand their reach and tap into India’s growing investor base across smaller cities and towns.

According to data compiled by Entrackr, wealthtech startups in India raised around $317 million across 26 deals in the first eight months of 2026. Funding activity was largely guided by smaller rounds, with only four transactions crossing the $30 million threshold. These included fundraises by Veriqus Group, Neo, Sahi, and Gurugram-based Centricity. Notably, none of the deals during the period exceeded $50 million, but this could change soon as Dale Vaz-led Sahi is reportedly in talks to raise a larger round of around $80 million. 
Meanwhile, Dream Sports, the parent company of Dream11, shut down its wealth management platform Dream Money within a year of its launch, ending one of its diversification bets beyond online gaming.
Year-on-year funding trend
India’s wealthtech sector saw moderate funding activity in 2023. Startups raised around $55 million across 12 deals, with Neo’s $35 million round accounting for a significant share of the capital raised during the year.
Funding picked up sharply in 2024. Capital raised jumped more than 3.4X to $265 million across 26 deals, supported by several sizable rounds.

The momentum continued in 2025. Funding rose around 40% year-on-year to $369.34 million across 25 deals, while the number of transactions remained broadly stable.
In the first eight months of 2026, wealthtech startups raised around $303 million across 25 deals. The sector has already surpassed the funding recorded in 2024, despite the 2026 figure covering only eight months.
Top funded startups in 2026
Most wealthtech funding rounds in 2026 were small-ticket deals raised by early-stage startups. However, a significant share of the capital was concentrated among a handful of companies. Mumbai-based Veriqus Group raised around $40 million in a funding round led by Norwest Venture Partners, while wealth and asset management firm Neo Group secured $36.3 million from existing investor Peak XV Partners.
Stock broking platform Sahi raised $33 million in a Series B round led by Accel, with participation from Elevation Capital. Centricity secured around $30 million in its Series A round led by SMBC Asia Rising Fund, while Bengaluru-based Stable Money raised nearly $39.3 million across two funding rounds from Fundamentum, Peak XV Partners, RTP Global, and Z47. Together, these five startups accounted for more than 56% of the total wealthtech funding raised in 2026.
Other notable fundraisers during the year included Wint Wealth, which raised $28 million in a Series B round, along with Nexedge Capital, AssetPlus, Oolka, and Bachatt.
Consolidations in the Wealthtech this year
Only four mergers and acquisitions have taken place in the wealthtech space so far in 2026, with three of them carried out by Raise Financial Services, the parent company of stockbroking platform Dhan.
In April, Raise acquired private market investment platform Infinyte Club and algorithmic trading platform Stratzy. A month later, it acquired IRDAI-registered GreenLife Insurance Broking (GIBL), which marked its entry into insurance distribution.
The fourth deal saw wealth management platform Scripbox acquire the mutual fund distribution business of Delhi-NCR-based Bluechip Capital, with its clients and employees set to transition to Scripbox.

Conclusion
India’s wealthtech funding surge points to a market entering a phase of development, but the next challenge is converting capital into durable businesses. The concentration of funding among a few larger players suggests investors remain selective, while smaller startups continue to test new models across wealth management, alternative investments and advisory. The bigger opportunity lies in expanding beyond metros and building products for India’s growing base of first-time investors.

Founded by Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal, Moneyview operates a digital lending and personal finance platform. The company offers personal loans and other financial products through its platform and works with lending partners.
The IPO size cut comes as a number of Indian fintech companies prepare to tap the public markets, with investors paying closer attention to profitability, growth and valuations.

title: Govt specifies no charges on UPI, RuPay debit card payments up to Rs 2,000
summary:
The Centre has specified that banks and payment system providers cannot impose charges on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions of up to Rs 2,000 or payments made using RuPay-powered debit cards.
The Finance Ministry, in a notification issued on Monday, said that “no bank or system provider shall impose, whether directly or indirectly, any charge” on a person making or receiving a payment through the specified electronic modes.
The electronic modes specified by the government include RuPay-powered debit cards and UPI transactions up to Rs 2,000. Both RuPay and UPI are managed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
For UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, the notification does not specify a no-charge provision, leaving scope for merchant discount rate (MDR) to be introduced on higher-value UPI transactions.
The notification follows the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026, which amended the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, to empower the Centre to specify electronic payment modes on which banks and system providers cannot levy charges.
The amendment, passed in August, replaced the earlier provision under which electronic modes notified under the Income-tax Act were protected from such charges. The amended law allows the government to specify the modes and transaction categories that will remain charge-free.
The amendment came amid discussions around a possible MDR framework for UPI. The government had clarified that the amendment itself did not impose any charge on UPI users. Any proposed MDR was expected to be limited to certain merchant transactions, while person-to-person (P2P) UPI payments would continue to remain free.
The latest notification now specifies UPI transactions up to Rs 2,000 and RuPay-powered debit card payments under the no-charge provision. It does not introduce an MDR or specify any rate for UPI transactions above Rs 2,000.

title: Lenskart increases stake in AjnaLens parent to 9% with Rs 8 Cr investment
summary:
Lenskart Solutions has increased its stake in AjnaLens’ parent company, Dimension NXG, to 9.01% after investing an additional Rs 8 crore in the extended reality (XR) startup.
The eyewear company acquired a 1.8% stake in Dimension NXG for Rs 7.99 crore, according to its regulatory filing. The transaction was completed on September 13, 2026.
This is Lenskart’s third stake purchase in Dimension NXG this year. It acquired an additional 0.68% stake in February and another 1.69% stake in July. With these three transactions, Lenskart’s stake in the company has increased from 4.84% to 9.01%.
The eyewear major has invested a total of Rs 18.5 crore to acquire the additional 4.17% stake through these transactions.
Lenskart said the investment will strengthen its strategic association with the XR, artificial intelligence (AI) and smart wearable technology ecosystem, while supporting technology-led opportunities in smart eyewear.
Lenskart first invested in AjnaLens in July 2025 to develop AI-powered smart glasses. The partnership combines Lenskart’s expertise in frame design and engineering with AjnaLens’ XR technology capabilities.
Founded in 2014 by Pankaj Raut, Abhijit Patil and Abhishek Tomar, AjnaLens develops hardware and software solutions using XR technology. The startup caters to sectors including defence and enterprises.
AjnaLens’ parent company reported a 35% decline in turnover to Rs 10.36 crore in FY26 from Rs 15.97 crore in FY24.
The latest investment comes as Lenskart steps up its focus on smart eyewear. The company has launched products such as Phonic audio glasses and is also working on AI-powered smart glasses. It has partnered with Qualcomm for the technology stack for its smart glasses.

title: Kissht parent OnEMI eyes fresh fundraise months after Rs 926 Cr IPO
summary:
OnEMI Technology Solutions, the parent company of digital lending platform Kissht, is considering another fundraise, just four months after its stock market debut in May.
The company’s board will meet on September 17 to consider raising funds through equity shares, warrants, convertible instruments or other eligible securities. The proposed fundraise could be carried out through a preferential issue, private placement or other permissible routes, according to a regulatory filing. The proposal will be subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals. 
The company, however, did not disclose the size of the proposed fundraise or the investors that may participate in the transaction.
The filing added that its trading window has been closed for designated persons and their immediate relatives and will remain shut until 48 hours after the board meeting outcome is announced. 
The development comes months after OnEMI raised Rs 926 crore through its initial public offering. The issue comprised a fresh issue of Rs 850 crore and an offer for sale of around Rs 76 crore by existing shareholders. 
On the financial front, Kissht’s operating revenue grew 45% year-on-year to Rs 670 crore in Q1 FY27, while its profit rose 58% to Rs 95 crore. Its assets under management (AUM) increased 61% YoY to Rs 8,001 crore during the quarter.
Kissht made its stock market debut in May, with its shares listing at Rs 190 on the NSE and Rs 191 on the BSE, over 11% above the issue price of Rs 171. Since then, the stock has surged over 72% to around Rs 329, which puts the company’s market capitalisation at Rs 5,830 crore.

title: Exclusive: Fashion startup UniqYou raises seed round at Rs 64 Cr valuation
summary:
D2C fashion startup UniqYou has raised Rs 15.8 crore in a seed funding round led by Arkam Ventures and Antler. The round also saw participation from several angel investors.
The board at UniqYou approved the issuance of 37,487 CCPS at an issue price of Rs 4,215 per share to raise the aforementioned amount, according to its regulatory filings.
Arkam Ventures invested Rs 9.3 crore in the round, followed by Antler with Rs 4.96 crore. Ankit Garg infused Rs 1 crore, while Abhishek Goyal, Chaitanya Ramalingegowda, Raveen Sastry, and Nandita Sinha also participated in the round.
A Moneycontrol report had earlier said that UniqYou was in talks to raise around Rs 12 crore ($1.3 million) in a funding round.

Following the allotment, Arkam Ventures will hold a 14.93% stake in UniqYou, while Antler will own 7.96%. Abhishek Goyal and Chaitanya Ramalingegowda will hold 1.59% and 0.24%, respectively.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, the company’s valuation stood at around Rs 64 crore (approximately $6.8 million) post-money. The fresh proceeds will be used to meet the company’s working capital needs and general corporate purposes, as per the filings.

Founded in 2026, UniqYou is a Bengaluru-based fashion startup focused on women’s fashion. The company is building a technology-led platform that leverages AI to identify emerging fashion trends and offer relevant products to consumers.
The fundraise comes amid continued investor interest in India’s fashion and apparel startup ecosystem. In 2025, The Bear House raised Rs 50 crore in a Series A round, while Snitch raised Rs 278.9 crore in a Series B round and Miraggio secured $6.5 million in Series A funding. The momentum continued in 2026, with MyDesignation raising Rs 40 crore in Series A funding and Alaya by Stage3 securing a seed round to scale its ethnic-wear business and AI capabilities. More recently, D2C fashion brand Theater raised Rs 75 crore in a Series A round led by Niveshaay.

title: Exclusive: PhysicsWallah founders, Udaan’s Sujeet Kumar to back Furnishka’s fresh fundraise
summary:
Furniture startup Furnishka is raising Rs 26.8 crore in an extended pre-Series A round, with PhysicsWallah founders Alakh Pandey and Prateek Boob, and Udaan co-founder Sujeet Kumar among the investors, according to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr. 
The Bengaluru-based company has issued 3,183 preference shares at an issue price of Rs 84,157 per share to raise the capital. 
The round saw participation from Beenext Asia, Bhaarath Sang, Onyx InVen, Amit Jain, Shantanu Jain, Manish Dugar, Mohit Gupta and Jnabiz Consulting, 
Bhaarath Sang will the largest investor in the round, investing Rs 10.3 crore. Beenext Asia will invest Rs 3.35 crore, while Onyx InVen and Amit Jain will invest Rs 2.37 crore each.
Mohit Gupta and Jnabiz Consulting are investing around Rs 2 crore each, while Sujeet Kumar will invest around Rs 1 crore. Alakh Pandey and Prateek Boob will invest Rs 1.14 crore each. Shantanu Jain and Manish Dugar will invest Rs 94.3 lakh and Rs 15.1 lakh, respectively.
This seems to be part of a larger round. Most of the money mentioned above has hit the bank account, while some will follow soon. Based on the issue price and the company's share capital, Entrackr estimates Furnishka’s post-money valuation at around Rs 230 crore.
With this round, Furnishka has raised Rs 70 crore so far. The company had earlier raised Rs 27 crore in a pre-Series A round led by IndiaQuotient in October 2024. Sparrow Capital and angel investors, including Udaan co-founder Sujeet Kumar and Ramakant Sharma, also participated in that round.
Founded in 2023 by Ganesh Pawar, Furnishka operates an omnichannel furniture retail business, combining online sales with large-format offline stores. The company offers furniture across living room, dining room, and bedroom categories, with a focus on customisation and supply-chain efficiencies.

title: Info Edge appoints ex-Adobe India MD to board, Himanshu Agarwal to take charge as CFO
summary:
Info Edge, the parent company of Naukri, has announced a leadership reshuffle, appointing Naresh Chand Gupta, former Managing Director of Adobe Systems India, as an independent director and Himanshu Agarwal as its new chief financial officer (CFO).
The former Adobe India MD will join Info Edge’s board from October 1 for a five-year term, subject to shareholder approval. He currently works with Accuracap Technologies and Accuracap Consultancy Services and serves as an independent director on the boards of eClerx Services and NoPaperForms. He had earlier served as an independent director at Info Edge until March 2023.
Meanwhile, Agarwal will take charge as CFO from September 17 and will also join the board as an additional director. He is set to become a whole-time director and CFO, subject to the required approvals.
Agarwal brings over three decades of experience across finance, corporate governance, mergers and acquisitions and business transformation at companies in India and overseas.
The leadership change will also see Ambarish Raghuvanshi step down as Info Edge’s interim CFO. Raghuvanshi, who has held the role since November 2025, will conclude his tenure on September 16.
However, he will continue to be associated with the company as a finance advisor until October 31 and will support the transition and handover to Agarwal.
Info Edge has also inducted Agarwal into its Risk Management Committee and Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting Committee.
The company said the leadership changes will strengthen its finance and leadership capabilities as it continues to focus on its internet businesses and technology investments.

title: iBRICS Summit 2026 concludes with focus on sovereign capital and cross-border payments
summary:
The inaugural iBRICS Summit 2026, organised by the Sovereign Wealth Fund Institute (SWFI), concluded in New Delhi after bringing together investors, policymakers and business leaders to discuss sovereign capital, cross-border payments and digital financial infrastructure.
The two-day summit culminated in the signing of the iBRICS DART Charter, which seeks to establish a framework for the coexistence, interoperability and regulation of central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) and private digital assets across the Global South.
The event brought together more than 500 institutional investors, finance ministers and business leaders representing a combined $1 trillion in sovereign wealth funds, public pension funds and family offices.
The summit saw participation from government, technology, healthcare and corporate sectors. Attendees included Naveen Jindal, chairman of Jindal Steel & Power; Ashish Jaiswal; Meenakshi Lekhi, former Union Minister of State for External Affairs and Culture; and Gurjeet Singh Aujla, Member of Parliament.
The healthcare sector was represented by Rajeev Sikka, chief information officer at Medanta. The delegation also included Rajshekhar Joshi, technologist and vice chairman of SETU Aayog.
“As we look toward future annual editions and expand SWFI's footprint—from our upcoming I-20 Investment Week in Dallas to future BRICS chairships—this Summit stands as the catalyst where sovereign capital shifted from passive allocation to actively shaping the economic plumbing of the Global South,” said Lakshmi Narayanan, chairman of SWFI and lead co-chair of iBRICS 2026.
The summit also focused on connecting sovereign capital with investment opportunities across infrastructure, clean energy, critical minerals and digital public infrastructure in the 21 BRICS member states and partner nations.
The event concluded with bilateral deal tables and sector-focused roundtables covering areas such as energy security, including petrochemicals, green hydrogen and carbon capture, along with logistics, sovereign computing, artificial intelligence and data security.
iBRICS is an annual sovereign investment and deal summit convened by SWFI on the sidelines of the BRICS Leaders’ Summit. The 2026 edition marked the inaugural edition of the summit.

title: Bengaluru Court restrains Way2News from using AppsForBharat’s confidential info and IP
summary:
The Bengaluru Commercial Court has restrained Way2News from using confidential information, intellectual property and data belonging to devotional technology startup AppsForBharat, giving the temporary company interim relief in its dispute with the operator of VedaMandir.
The copy of order reviewed by Entrackr was passed on September 10 by the LXXXVII Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge in a commercial suit filed by FirstPrinciple AppsForBharat against Way2News. 
The court, after hearing the counsel for AppsForBharat, granted an ad-interim ex parte injunction restraining Way2News, its directors, employees, agents and representatives from using any confidential information belonging to AppsForBharat, including intellectual property and any other data generated by the company and received from its former employee , Shivam Kumar Singh. 
The matter is next listed for October 5 for further proceedings. The injunction is temporary and remains in force until the next hearing.
The dispute centres on VedaMandir, Way2News’s recently launched devotional platform that allows users to book personalised chadhava, pujas and daan at temples, with documentation and prasad delivery. AppsForBharat has operated Sri Mandir since December 2020, a competing platform that offers digital devotional services and connects devotees with temples and priests.
AppsForBharat has alleged that Way2News illegally obtained and used its confidential business information and intellectual property. A key part of its case concerns Sri Mandir’s videos that it says were used by Way2News on VedaMandir’s social media and in its marketing campaigns on or around August 31. According to the suit, those videos are the intellectual property of AppsForBharat and had originally been uploaded to AppsForBharat’s Google Drive and internal systems on March 18. The company submitted screenshots and comparisons of the material to the court.
AppsForBharat also placed before the court an August 25 confidential data access attempt from an account using the Way2News domain. The request sought access to a folder containing its user data and video material and was sent from the official Way2News email address of its former employee. The company described the request as an attempt to access sensitive proprietary information and trade secrets.
Way2News, in its response to AppsForBharat’s allegations, denied any attempt to access or use confidential information. It said the disputed Google Drive access resulted from an old link connected to Singh’s previous employment. According to Way2News, Singh inadvertently accessed the link, realised he was still part of legacy WhatsApp groups from his previous workplace and exited them. The company said there was no intent to obtain, transfer or use AppsForBharat’s confidential information.
Way2News also said it had not received any court order so far.
The startup has also relied on confidentiality obligations in the former employee’s agreement, which covered business, technical, financial, customer, supplier and marketing information. It has sought permanent injunctions against the use or disclosure of its confidential information and intellectual property, return of such material, an account of profits, and Rs 1 crore in compensation.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Sep 07 - Sep 12]
summary:
This week, 23 Indian startups raised $356.8 million across six growth-stage deals, 17 early-stage deals, and two undisclosed rounds. The week also recorded five key appointments, one departure, two mergers and acquisitions, and a new fund launch.

In contrast, 25 startups had collectively secured about $303.7 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised $182 million across six deals this week. Bengaluru-based restaurant company Popo Global led the pack with $56 million from Artal Asia, followed by women’s wellness brand Nua, which raised $50 million in a Series C round led by Peak XV Partners.
Workforce accommodation startup HerSpace Manufacturing secured a $40 million commitment from Gray Matters Capital, while quick food delivery startup Swish raised $24 million led by Bertelsmann India Investments. Fleet management platform Carrum Mobility raised $10 million in a Series B round led by Uber, while pet food brand Lickicious secured Rs 19 crore led by Prath Ventures.
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $174.8 million across 15 deals this week. Space-tech startup Pixxel led the pack with a $100 million Series C round co-led by Temasek and Seraphim Space, followed by cybersecurity firm QNu Labs, which raised Rs 200 crore in a Series A1 round co-led by the National Quantum Mission and Speciale Invest.
Cardless payments platform Piston raised $15 million in a Series A round led by FPV Ventures, while AI-powered patient safety startup Graph AI secured $13.3 million led by Insight Partners. Fashion brand Theater raised Rs 75 crore at a Rs 410 crore post-money valuation, while Cooling-as-a-Service platform Circolife secured $4.5 million.
Other funded startups included voice AI startup Navana.ai, B2B pharma distribution platform Fundly.ai, AI-powered water infrastructure firm DigitalPaani, and several others. YoLearn.ai, SpeakX, Neurotech and deeptech firm BQP also raised capital, with amounts undisclosed.
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru led the funding charts with 14 startup deals during the week, followed by Delhi-NCR with four. Mumbai, Thane and Kerala also recorded deals.

AI startups led the sectors with five deals, followed by foodtech, healthtech, fintech, F&B and deeptech with two deals each, while spacetech, proptech, mobility, e-commerce and other sectors also saw funding activity.
[Series-wise deals]
Series A and seed rounds led the week with seven deals each, followed by Series B, pre-seed and undisclosed rounds with two deals each. Series C and pre-Series A recorded one deal each.

[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding increased over 17% to $356.8 million from $303.7 million raised in the previous week.
The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $232.37 million across 21 deals.
[Key Hirings / Departures]
Enterprise software startup Whatfix appointed co-founder Vara Kumar as CEO, effective immediately, following the demise of co-founder Khadim Batti on September 1. NIIF appointed Gauravjit Singh as managing partner and global head of capital formation.
Bhartiya Converge named Eric Pagdiwalla as chief operating officer, while Honasa Consumer elevated Nishchay Bahl to chief business officer, offline.
Ajit Mohan stepped down as Snap’s chief business officer and will return to Singapore to spend more time with his family. Snap named EMEA President Ronan Harris as chief commercial officer.
[Mergers and Acquisitions]
Swiggy has agreed to sell its retail distribution business Lynk Logistics to B2B e-commerce platform Udaan for Rs 500 crore. Meanwhile, Kochi-based Cyrix Healthcare has acquired the MedTech Solutions business of Blue Star Engineering & Electronics.
[Fund launches]
Healthcare-focused venture firm W Health Ventures (WHV) has closed its second fund at Rs 700 crore, oversubscribing its initial target of Rs 630 crore. The fund plans to build 8–10 healthcare companies from the pre-idea stage to category leaders over the next four years.
[New launches and partnerships]
▪️ Multipl launches spending app on UPI, targets two lakh users and Rs 200 crore in 12 months
▪️ Agnikul Cosmos expands infrastructure for reusable rocket testing
▪️ Upstox launches US stocks investing, opens access to 8,000+ US stocks and 2,000+ ETFs
▪️ PB Pay launches payment aggregation platform for businesses
▪️ Sarvam, Mahindra Finance expand Voice AI partnership across sales, collections and employee engagement
▪️ Xflow partners with HSBC to launch India collections for global businesses
[News flash this week]
▪️ Zomato, Swiggy deliver near-Meituan unit economics despite 22X smaller Indian market
▪️ Flipkart Minutes clocks 4X growth in two years, expands to more than 150 cities
▪️ Groww adds 2.23 lakh active clients in August; Sahi clocks 11% growth
▪️ RNFI Services receives RBI in-principle authorisation to operate as a Payment Aggregator – Physical
[Summary]
On a weekly basis, startup funding surged over 39% to $303.7 million from $218.7 million raised in the previous week.
India’s food delivery market is nearly 22X smaller than China’s, yet Zomato and Swiggy are already close to Chinese giant Meituan on key unit economics. While Meituan operates at a vastly larger scale, it generated around $0.3 in operating profit per order at its peak in Q2 2024, compared with around $0.2 in adjusted EBITDA per order for Zomato and Swiggy in Q1 FY27, according to Bernstein.
Flipkart Minutes has completed two years of operations, with the quick commerce platform growing 4X year-on-year and expanding to nearly 1,200 micro-fulfilment centres across over 150 cities. Around 60% of its customers return to the platform, while its customer base across Tier II and smaller cities has grown nearly 25X year-on-year.
Consumer fintech platform Multipl has launched a UPI-based spending account that allows users to keep money for everyday expenses invested in liquid mutual funds until needed. The launch follows a pilot with over 20,000 users and Rs 20 crore in investments, along with around Rs 4 crore in UPI transactions. Multipl plans to scale the product to about 2 lakh users and Rs 200 crore in investments over the next six to 12 months.
Agnikul Cosmos has opened two new units at its Chennai facility to test reusable rocket stages under flight-like conditions and manufacture key launch vehicle components in-house. The facilities were inaugurated in the presence of Gaganyaan astronaut Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla.
RNFI Services has received in-principle authorisation from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to operate as a Payment Aggregator – Physical (PA-P). The approval will allow the company to expand into physical, offline and in-store payments, subject to fulfilment of RBI’s requirements for final authorisation.
Upstox has launched US stock investing on its platform, allowing Indian users to invest in over 8,000 US-listed stocks and more than 2,000 ETFs directly through its app. The offering also supports fractional investing, with investments starting from as little as $1.
PB Fintech’s payment aggregator platform PB Pay has launched operations and is now open for merchant sign-ups and transaction processing. Licensed by the RBI in February 2026, the platform allows merchants to accept multiple payment modes through a single integration and dashboard.
Mahindra Finance has expanded its voice AI partnership with Bengaluru-based Sarvam across sales, collections and employee engagement. Voice agents developed by Mahindra AI on Sarvam’s platform operate across 12 Indian languages and have completed over one crore customer calls to date.
At Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026, cross-border payments platform Xflow partnered with HSBC to enable global businesses to collect payments from Indian customers through cards, net banking and UPI, without setting up a local entity in India.

summary:
Furniture and appliance rental platform RentoMojo’s Rs 1,256 crore IPO saw strong investor demand, with the issue subscribed 72.87 times on the final day of bidding.
According to exchange data, the qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) portion led the demand, with bids worth 177.3 times the shares on offer. The non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 67.92 times, followed by the employee portion at 21 times and the retail quota at 15.58 times.
The IPO opened for subscription on September 9 at a price band of Rs 384-404 per share. The issue comprises a fresh issue of Rs 150 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) worth Rs 1,105.6 crore by existing shareholders.
Ahead of the IPO, which opened on September 9, RentoMojo raised Rs 376.07 crore from anchor investors. The anchor round saw participation from domestic mutual funds, insurance companies, and pension funds. Key participants included Kotak, ICICI Prudential Quality Fund, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock Global Funds, HDFC Mutual Fund and others.
Founded in 2014, Bengaluru-based RentoMojo operates a subscription-based rental platform for furniture, appliances and other household products. It competes with players such as Furlenco and Cityfurnish.
At the upper end of the price band, the company is seeking a valuation of around $444 million. The fresh issue proceeds will be used towards debt repayment and other corporate purposes.
RentoMojo’s revenue from operations grew 45.5% to Rs 387 crore in FY26, while its profit surged 142% to Rs 104 crore during the fiscal year.
The IPO is being managed by Motilal Oswal, Axis Capital and IIFL Capital Services. RentoMojo shares are expected to list on the NSE and BSE on September 17.

title: NPCI’s FY26 profit falls 32%; revenue rises 22% to Rs 4,240 Cr
summary:
The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), which operates retail payment services such as UPI, IMPS, RuPay, BHIM, NACH, FASTag and BBPS, recorded a 22% year-on-year rise in revenue in FY26. However, its profit fell 32% during the year due to higher deferred tax and a rise in marketing expenses, including cashbacks and sponsorships.
NPCI’s revenue from operations rose 22% to Rs 4,240 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026 from Rs 3,481 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated annual financial statements accessed by Entrackr from its website.

Established in 2008 as an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Indian Banks’ Association (IBA), NPCI serves as the umbrella organisation for retail payment and settlement systems in India. It operates key payment platforms and services such as UPI, IMPS, RuPay, BHIM, NACH, AePS, FASTag and BBPS. As NPCI operates as a not-for-profit organisation, it reports its profit as surplus.
Payment services remained NPCI’s primary revenue driver in FY26, contributing 88% of its operating revenue. Income from this segment rose 16% to Rs 3,736 crore from Rs 3,212 crore in FY25. The remaining operating income came from certification, network and implementation charges, membership fees, hologram charges and card-related fees.
NPCI also earned Rs 633 crore from non-operating sources in FY26, which took its total income to Rs 4,873 crore. Other income included liabilities written back, interest on income tax refunds, service guarantee mechanism (SGM) receipts, and miscellaneous income.
When it comes to expenses, Marketing and product incentives remained NPCI's largest cost centre in FY26, accounting for over 47% of its overall expenditure. These expenses rose 27% to Rs 1,420 crore from Rs 1,116 crore in FY25, led by higher spending on product incentives and cashbacks.
Marketing costs also included payments to banks for RuPay cards, advertising and publicity campaigns, B2B activities, and sponsorships.
Employee benefit expenses rose over 22% to Rs 534 crore in FY26, while depreciation and amortisation costs increased 40% to Rs 408 crore. Operating expenses also grew 39% to Rs 291 crore from Rs 210 crore in FY25, driven by higher annual maintenance charges for network and IT equipment, network expenses, and data centre costs.
Other expenses, including travel, professional fees, training and seminars, also added to NPCI’s cost base during the year. Overall, the corporation’s expenditure grew 32% to Rs 2,985 crore in FY26 from Rs 2,270 crore in FY25.
As expenses outpaced revenue growth, the firm's bottom line came under pressure in FY26. Higher spending on marketing, product incentives and cashbacks, coupled with a deferred tax expense of Rs 331 crore, led its surplus to decline 32% to Rs 991 crore from Rs 1,461 crore in FY25.

It's EBITDA rose 11% to Rs 1,674 crore in FY26, with an EBITDA margin of 39.5%. Its ROCE stood at 12.9%. On a unit level, the corporation spent Rs 0.70 to earn a rupee of operating revenue during the year.
At the end of March 2026, NPCI’s had total current assets of Rs 8,081 crore with a healthy cash and bank balance of Rs 6,119 crore.
